messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Incident P1 opened — high tail latency affecting hosted inference endpoints (streaming stalls). Paging on-call.

alex: oncall-ml you're up — seeing p95/p99 jumps in the metrics dashboard, streaming consumers complaining about stalls. I can start gathering traces.

oncall-ml: ack, looking. Alerts: p95 ~ 1.3s -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 200ms -> 2.6s for text-generation.v2. Streaming tail errors: increased send timeouts, clients see chunk delays. No error spike in model process yet.

maria: I see a correlated spike in auth service 429s and config-fetch latency (control-plane). auth-svc 95th latency ~350ms -> 1.2s, plus rate-limit responses. Config service shows many retries to DB.

simon: interesting — control-plane dependencies like auth/token and feature-config fetch are on the hot path for inference right now (we fetch flags + customer config per request for routing). If those are slow, we add tail latency.

jade: any customer-facing impact? product-ops, can you surface if any paying customers reported errors?

product-ops: a few support tickets from two customers about streaming stalls, also automated SLO alerting flagged >5% request latency breach for some orgs.

alex: quick mitigation checklist — let's try to (1) route reads to cached configs, (2) increase auth service rate limit for critical routing tokens, (3) enable circuit breaker on config fetch to return last-known-good. Who can flip the feature-flag rollback?

maria: I can bump auth-svc replicas and temporarily raise token rate bucket for internal controlplane traffic. Doing that now.

maria: (command) kubectl scale deployment auth-svc -n controlplane --replicas=6

oncall-ml: I'm enabling fallback cache for config fetch on the proxy layer. Patch applied to edge-proxy config to return cached config if fetch > 300ms.

oncall-ml: (snippet)
```
edge-proxy:
  config_fetch_timeout_ms: 300
  on_timeout: serve_cached
```

simon: we'll also disable per-request feature flag evaluation for hosted-api route until config backend stabilizes. jade — can you roll that back? It's the routing.flags.eval flag for hosted-api.

jade: on it. Flipping flag now via admin-console UI. Confirming: routing.flags.eval = false for hosted-api org-agnostic.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollout of edge-proxy config to 3/3 hosts successful. auth-svc autoscale event: +2 replicas complete.

alex: any immediate effect on p99?

oncall-ml: yes, within 90s p95 down to ~600ms and p99 to ~900ms. Streaming stalls decreasing. Customers still see intermittent stalls for in-flight sessions, but new sessions look healthier.

maria: partial root cause: our auth service started hitting an internal rate-limiter due to an unexpected surge of control-plane telemetry from a misbehaving batch job. That caused throttling and longer retries which propagated as tail latency.

simon: can we temporarily bypass remote token validation for existing sessions (validate locally cache) to avoid extra auth RPCs for streaming chunk sends?

maria: yes we have a short-lived token cache on the gateway. Enabling aggressive token-cache hit window + local validation for 10m.

maria: (command)
```
gatewayctl set token_cache_ttl 600 --scope hosted-api
```

oncall-ml: also adding a breaker on config DB queries so a surge doesn't starve worker threads. Reduced DB connection pool for controlplane to protect inference path.

oncall-ml: (log snippet)
```
[proxy] config-fetch START req_id=abcd
[proxy] config-fetch WARNING slow: 420ms
[proxy] config-fetch SERVED_CACHED req_id=abcd
```

jade: folks — rolling back routing.flags.eval didn't require code change, flag toggle completed. Monitoring for regressions.

sre-bot: grafana alert resolved: inference.p99_above_threshold cleared at 1778501502.

alex: good. Remaining action items: (a) find and stop the batch job flood that triggered auth rate limits, (b) add long-term token-caching for streaming, (c) add circuit-breaker defaults + better latency budget docs for control-plane dependencies, (d) customer communications for impacted orgs. Simon / Maria / Jade, can one of you own the RCA?

simon: I'll own RCA and follow-up tickets. Initial theory: misconfigured batch job from analytics team started spamming control-plane auth token ops. I'll open the postmortem and link infra logs.

maria: I'll coordinate with infra to tighten rate-limiter defaults and add a hard quota for controlplane telemetry. Also adding a k8s HPA for auth-svc based on request latency, not just CPU.

jade: I'll draft a short customer note for the impacted accounts and post it in #customer-notifications for signoff.

product-ops: flagging impacted orgs and ETA for follow-up. Recommend offering extended logs for any customers who saw stalls.

alex: handing to simon for RCA. oncall-ml and Maria — please continue monitoring for 30m and then hand to eng-sre for long-term mitigation tracking.

oncall-ml: handing to eng-sre @sre-team. I'll add context to the incident ticket and include the commands we ran.

simon: created incident ticket INC-2026-241 in Jira, linked this thread and flagged P1 -> P2 transition after mitigations. Will post timeline and next steps in the ticket once root cause confirmed.

alex: thanks everyone. Great async coordination. Please keep this thread updated with any regressions.

inc-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 30m.

sre-bot: note: long-term followups created: FW-430 (token cache redesign), INF-512 (control-plane rate-limiter tighten), DOCS-88 (latency budget for control-plane deps).
